prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1268; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the insured reporting a low-speed head-on collision at a residential intersection. The claimant is the other driver and has retained counsel, so all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was in force at the time of the reported loss. No issues with policy status were found.

Entry 3: Obtained photographs of both vehicles from the scene and statements from two independent witnesses. Both witnesses describe the vehicles meeting nose to nose at low speed, consistent with the insured's account.

Entry 4: Spoke with the other driver, who gave the same description of how the collision happened. Their account matches the witness statements and the scene photos.

Entry 5: Reviewed the damage photos with our appraiser. The damage pattern is mostly in line with the described impact, and no prior damage to the vehicle is known from our records or the repair history.

Entry 6: Received the medical records and claim package from the attorney's office. The claimant reports a wrist fracture, which fits the kind of force expected from a collision of this type.

Entry 7: Treatment has run somewhat longer than is typical for this injury, so the file has been flagged for a standard review of the treatment plan and billing.

Entry 8: Requested prior medical history from the claimant through counsel. No earlier injury to the same wrist or arm has been identified in the records received so far.

Entry 9: Spoke with the claimant's attorney, who confirmed the client is still following the treatment plan. The claimant has given the same account of the accident in every conversation we have had.

Entry 10: Noted that the seating position of the claimant at the time of impact is not yet fully clear from the statements and photos. Asked counsel to confirm seat position for the file.

Entry 11: Nothing so far suggests the damage predates the policy start date. The file remains open pending the treatment review and the seat position confirmation.
